sections.title: Surviving Rochester: The Winter & Summer
sections.summary: Rochester weather has range. This section collects advice on winter gear, summer routines, groceries, transit, housing, and the small habits that make the city easier.
prompts: What winter gear was actually worth buying?
How do you handle campus movement in snow?
What summer spots helped you breathe?

experiences.name: Anonymous
experiences.experience: Buy waterproof boots before the first real snow, not after. A warm coat matters, but gloves, wool socks, and a hat make the daily walk feel much less dramatic.

prompts: Where did you find a familiar flavor?
What should new students order first?
Which grocery items are easy to miss?

experiences.name: BSA Food Team
experiences.experience: Keep a shared map of halal restaurants, South Asian groceries, and late-night options. Add notes about spice level, price, and whether it is easy to reach without a car.

sections.title: Finance Advice
sections.kicker: Credit, income rules, and careful starts
sections.summary: You can own a business and stocks, but you cannot work for them if your visa status does not allow it. Build credit slowly, avoid minimum-only payments, and ask before taking paid work.
prompts: How did you start building credit?
What money mistake should others avoid?
Which campus office helped clarify employment rules?

experiences.name: Anonymous alum
experiences.experience: For a first credit card, use it for one predictable bill and pay the full statement balance every month. Credit building is easy when utilization stays low and payments are never late.

sections.title: Immigration Advice
sections.summary: Collect practical reminders about ISO appointments, I-20 updates, travel signatures, CPT, OPT, SSN timing, and when to talk to a qualified advisor instead of guessing. Featured resource: ImmiGenius for the path to a Green Card in the US.

links.label: ImmiGenius: Path to a US Green Card

prompts: What deadline surprised you?
What should students prepare before travel?
Which documents do you keep scanned?

experiences.name: Community note
experiences.experience: Before international travel, check your passport validity, visa stamp, I-20 travel signature, enrollment status, and any pending immigration applications. Email ISO early.

sections.title: Academic Challenges

sections.summary: Notes on office hours, TA support, writing help, group projects, course loads, add/drop decisions, and adapting to a different academic culture.

How did you recover from a rough first exam?

experiences.name: Anonymous
experiences.experience: Office hours are not only for emergencies. Going early helped me understand what professors expected, and it made asking for help feel normal before grades became stressful.

sections.title: Research Challenges
sections.summary: A space for research group expectations, emailing professors, finding projects, handling rejection, reading papers, presenting work, and staying motivated.
prompts: How did you find your first lab?
What made advisor communication better?
How do you organize papers and experiments?

experiences.name: Graduate student
experiences.experience: When emailing a professor, mention one specific paper or project and explain your relevant skills in two short paragraphs. Follow up once after a week.

experiences.name: Anonymous
experiences.experience: Ask senior students about rides before big religious events. Many people are happy to coordinate, but it helps everyone if plans start a few days early.
